steps.intro: Meet the sounds and shapes of Hebrew before any rules. Read each line aloud, then check the English. Capital letters show the stressed syllable.

cards.title: Aleph with Beth, lesson 1
cards.note: Optional: a short lesson taught entirely in Biblical Hebrew, with pictures. Come back here when it ends.

cards.title: Hebrew reads right to left
body: Start at the right-hand edge and read towards the left. The letters are consonants; most of the small dots and dashes above and below them are the vowels.
You will learn the 22 letters and the vowels one at a time in the first lessons. For now, follow the pronunciation guide.

cards.title: Small words join on to the front
body: “In”, “the” and “and” are single letters fixed to the front of the next word: בְּ (in), הַ or הָ (the), וְ (and).
The verb often comes first: בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים is “created God”, meaning “God created”. The little word אֵת marks what was created and is not translated.

cards.explain: אֱלֹהִים (e-lo-HIM) is God. It looks plural, but with the singular verb בָּרָא it means the one God.

cards.prompt: Which letter means “the” in הַשָּׁמַיִם (the heavens)?
cards.explain: הַ at the front (the right-hand end) means “the”.

cards.prompt: Match each Hebrew word to its meaning.
Put the words in order: “In the beginning God created”. Remember, Hebrew starts on the right.
cards.explain: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים: “in the beginning”, then the verb “created”, then “God”.
בָּרָא is “he created”: one person, a finished action. Grammar books call this the Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, written 3ms.

steps.intro: Now read the real verses. Words you have met are underlined in gold; tap any word to see what it means.

cards.note: This verse looks back on Genesis 1. Find הַשָּׁמַיִם and הָאָרֶץ near the start, and בְּהִבָּרְאָם: “when they were created”, from the same root as בָּרָא.
